title: Step 2A: Make ritual history truly multi-day (append-only per couple per day)

requirements.text: Update the backend ritual storage model so ritual entries are stored append-only per coupleId AND per day (e.g., a unique key derived from coupleId + day number), instead of overwriting a single entry per coupleId. Ensure that submitting a ritual response for the same couple on the same day updates the same day’s entry (merging responses by userId), and submitting on a different day creates a new entry without affecting prior days.

quotes: please proceed with implementing the updated step 2A.

acceptanceCriteria: Two different calendar days for the same couple produce two distinct stored ritual entries (prior day is not overwritten).
Two submissions on the same day (caller + partner) both appear in the same day’s stored entry under that couple.
Ritual response merging remains keyed by userId so a user re-submitting updates only their own response for that day.

requirements.text: Update backend endpoints that currently assume a single ritual entry per couple so they work with the new per-day storage: (1) getRitualStatus must reflect today’s ritual completion status for the couple (based on today’s day key), and (2) getRitualHistory(limit) must return a list of RitualEntryView across multiple days, sorted reliably by date (newest first) and respecting the provided limit argument.

quotes: Add per-day keys: store ritual entries under coupleId + date instead of overwriting.
Update getRitualHistory to return all entries, sorted, respecting limit.

acceptanceCriteria: getRitualStatus returns completion for the current day only (not a previous day) and remains correct for partnerA/partnerB canonical attribution.
getRitualHistory(limit) returns at most `limit` entries when more exist.
getRitualHistory(limit) returns entries sorted newest-first using the entry.date field.
Existing behavior for unpaired users remains unchanged (traps/authorization as before).

requirements.text: Update the frontend data flow (React Query + any consuming UI) to match the backend’s multi-entry ritual history behavior, ensuring the Home and Memories pages correctly display multiple days and still treat ritualHistory[0] as the latest entry because results are sorted newest-first and limited.

quotes: Update frontend hook to match new response shape.

acceptanceCriteria: Home page ‘Ritual History’ section can show multiple entries across different days without regressions.
Memories page ‘Load More’ continues to work by increasing the limit and receiving more (older) entries from getRitualHistory(limit).
Home page ‘Both completed!’ section uses the latest entry (index 0) and shows the responses for today when today is complete.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor; implement Step 2A changes in backend/main.mo.

Do not edit files under frontend/immutablePaths (e.g., frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts(x), frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, frontend/src/components/ui). Compose or adjust code elsewhere if needed.
Do not implement Step 2B (streak/harmony/trends/badges computation) as part of this build.
nonGoals: Implementing real Insights computations (streaks, harmony math, trends) and badge unlock logic (Step 2B).
Adding new UI features beyond what is required to support multi-day ritual history display and correct ‘today’ status.
Introducing external databases or backend services.
